---
title: "Learning from a sample"
---

The foundations chapter separated the [unit of analysis and estimand](../foundations/making-sense-of-data.qmd). Statistical inference asks what observed speakers, tokens, items, or measurements can tell us about that estimand beyond the realized sample.

One dataset is only one possible result of a sampling process. A different set of speakers or sentence items would usually produce a different numerical summary, so an inferential procedure must state which sources of variation it represents.

## The frequentist sequence

The first part of this module develops frequentist inference in a fixed order.

1. [Populations and samples](populations-and-samples.qmd) specifies the units and population targeted by a linguistic claim.
2. [Independent sampling](independent-sampling.qmd) states one probability model connecting population parameters to repeated observations.
3. [A corpus proportion](pronoun-case-example.qmd) applies that model to one teaching extract.
4. [Maximum likelihood](maximum-likelihood.qmd) selects a parameter value by comparing the probability assigned to the observed sample.
5. [Sampling distributions](properties-of-estimators.qmd) study the estimation rule across possible samples.
6. [Standard errors](standard-errors.qmd), [bias](estimator-bias.qmd), and [mean squared error](mean-squared-error.qmd) describe different properties of that sampling distribution.
7. [Confidence intervals](confidence-intervals.qmd) and [exact binomial intervals](exact-binomial-intervals.qmd) construct procedures with repeated-sampling coverage.
8. [Null hypotheses and test statistics](null-hypotheses-and-test-statistics.qmd) compare an observed discrepancy with a declared reference distribution.
9. The remaining pages instantiate those ideas for one mean, paired measurements, independent means, and contingency tables.

Each step adds one object. A parameter is not an estimate, an estimator is not its realized value, and a confidence procedure is not a probability distribution over the fixed parameter.

## One file can support different targets

Suppose a corpus file contains 600 relative clauses from 30 speakers. The proportion of subject relatives among those 600 clauses is a property of the file. The average speaker-specific proportion is a different summary because every speaker receives equal weight. A population proportion for speakers in a region is different again because it extends beyond the sampled speakers.

These quantities may all be useful, but they are not interchangeable. The file alone does not select among them. The research question identifies the target, and the sampling design determines which observations supply independent information about it. Statistical machinery enters only after those choices have been made explicit.

This order prevents a common inferential shortcut: selecting a familiar procedure from the shape of a data table and deciding what its result means afterward. We will instead write the population quantity first, define an estimator second, and then study that estimator under a stated sampling model.

## The Bayesian branch

The later Bayesian branch begins from a probability model for observations and adds a probability distribution over unknown parameters. Bayes' rule then produces a posterior distribution. Predictive distributions connect parameter uncertainty back to possible observations.

Some posterior calculations are analytic. Others require simulation. Those computational pages occur only after the target posterior quantities have been defined.

## Population, sampling model, and procedure

For every inferential result, ask:

1. What population quantity is the target?
2. What sampling model connects that target to the observations?
3. What procedure turns one realized sample into the reported result?

Many misinterpretations collapse two of these questions. A precisely calculated standard error under the wrong unit of independence, for instance, remains a standard error for the wrong sampling model.

The [chapter dependency graph](../learning-path.qmd) shows which earlier chapters this chapter assumes. Begin by specifying the [population and sample](populations-and-samples.qmd).
